title: Coptic Calendar
intro: The Coptic calendar is used by Egypt's Coptic Christian tradition. It has a regular pattern of twelve thirty-day months and a very short thirteenth month, with an extra day in a leap year.
summary: Thirteen months; twelve have 30 days, the last has 5 or 6.
epoch: Year 1 of the Anno Martyrum (A.M.) era begins in AD 284, associated with the reign of Diocletian. The New Year is called Nayrouz.
year_rule: Months 1 through 12 have 30 days each. Month 13, Nasie, contains five days in ordinary years and six in Coptic leap years. The year follows the Alexandrian four-year leap cycle.
after_note: The five or six days of Nasie complete the year. A Coptic date is not simply a Gregorian date with a different year number.
history: The calendar developed from the Alexandrian reform of the older Egyptian civil year and remains important in Coptic Orthodox life and the agricultural seasons of Egypt. Its year numbers use the Era of the Martyrs rather than the Common Era.
limits: This guide describes the Coptic/Alexandrian model, not ancient Egyptian regnal dates. Month-name spellings vary by transliteration, and Julian/Gregorian date correspondences shift.
comparison_bottom: NASIE  /  LEAP YEAR ADDS ONE DAY
